result:
I could not fully verify the claimed lower bound, so this verdict rests on partial checks.

The construction is consistent. On $\Theta_1\times\Theta_2 \cong C_1\times C_2$ with $C_i$ of genus 2, a divisor of class $p_1^*(\alpha\text{ pts})+p_2^*(\beta\text{ pts})$ has genus $1+\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta$ by adjunction. For $(\alpha,\beta)=(2,2)$ this gives $1+4+4=9$, so the stated example does have genus 9.

The harder part is the minimality claim, which is a statement about all curves on $A_1\times A_2$, not only those on $\Theta_1\times\Theta_2$. I could not confirm that no curve of smaller genus exists. My recollection of the literature on this question is uncertain, and I cannot rule out a lower value.

VERDICT: ACCEPT

CONFIDENCE: 3
